question: Do words that swing, flip or fly in now look like they turn in space?
context: Reel: queue/audits/2026-10-11-text-depth-contact.png (clip Flip on top for comparison) and one MP4 and GIF per entrance by word and by letter beside it; WebKit before and after of the mock: queue/audits/2026-10-11-text-depth-mock-webkit-before-after.png. Already built at Next defaults; this card only tunes the strength.

options.label: Keep this strength
options.summary: Words and letters turn with the perspective in the new reel: half way in, the near edge of a turning word is about 1.3 to 1.6 times its far edge, and a word flipping toward you may grow a little past its text box.
pros: Depth reads at a glance, by word and by letter alike
Every word turns the same way wherever it sits on the line, with no italic lean
cons: Tilt Settle turns on two axes at once, so it still leans a little as it settles
options.mitigation: Tilt Settle can be made to tip only, if the lean bothers you.

options.label: Stronger: a closer camera on every word
options.summary: The same moves seen from even closer, so half way in a turning word has a near edge about twice its far one and swings in more dramatically.
cons: Words reach further past their text box and can look distorted at the start of a flip
options.mitigation: The camera distance is one number and can be tuned back.

options.label: Softer: the camera further back
options.summary: The moves keep their angles but foreshorten less: half way in the near edge is about 1.15 times the far one, closer to how they looked before.
pros: Calmer, closer to a subtle corporate title
cons: Comes back toward the flat look you rejected
options.mitigation: A title can still pick Swing In from a larger angle for more depth.
